title: Document and filing types: what each holds, how often, and how late
note: Read by the planning skill so the planner can name the right document and the period it covers before any search. `period_kind` says what one document spans; `lag_days` is the usual longest gap between the end of that period and the filing (US rules; the largest filers are fastest, small ones may take longer), used only to estimate which document is the newest by now. Fiscal calendars differ by company, so the estimate is a hint and the filing's own 'period of report' wins. Not legal advice.

documents.label: Form 10-K, annual report
documents.route_when: \b(10-?K|annual report|full[- ]year|fiscal year|annual (?:revenue|results|net income)|risk factors?|business overview|number of employees|headcount|properties)\b
documents.holds: business description, risk factors, management discussion, audited financial statements for the fiscal year, and exhibits (subsidiaries, material contracts)
documents.lag_note: due 60 days after the fiscal year end for the largest filers, 75 for mid-size, 90 for the rest
documents.tip: The fourth quarter has no 10-Q: its figures are in the 10-K and the earnings 8-K.

documents.label: Form 10-Q, quarterly report
documents.route_when: \b(10-?Q|quarterly|latest (?:\w+ )?(?:net sales|revenues?|earnings|results|net income)|last quarter|latest quarter|three months ended|nine months ended|Q[1-3]\b|quarter ended)\b
documents.holds: unaudited financial statements and management discussion for the first three fiscal quarters (year-to-date figures included)
documents.lag_note: due 40 days after the quarter end for the largest filers, 45 for the rest
documents.tip: Only three per fiscal year; the fourth quarter appears in the 10-K.

documents.label: Form 8-K, current report
documents.route_when: \b(8-?K|announced|announces|results of operations|earnings release|acquisition|completed the acquisition|material agreement|appointed|resign(?:ed|s|ation)|departure|stepped down|new (?:ceo|cfo)|shareholder vote|annual meeting results|bankruptcy|delist)\b
documents.holds: an event, filed within four business days. Items: 1.01 material agreement; 2.01 acquisition or disposal completed; 2.02 results of operations (the earnings release, usually Exhibit 99.1); 5.02 departure or appointment of a director or senior officer; 5.07 shareholder vote results; 7.01 and 8.01 other disclosures; 9.01 exhibits
documents.lag_note: four business days after the event
documents.tip: The event date and the filing date differ; give both.

documents.label: Proxy statement (DEF 14A)
documents.route_when: \b(DEF ?14A|proxy (?:statement)?|executive (?:pay|compensation)|ceo pay|say[- ]on[- ]pay|shareholder proposals?|annual meeting|board (?:members|composition)|director independence|letter to (?:share|stock)holders|shareholder letter)\b
documents.holds: annual meeting agenda, director nominees and biographies, executive pay tables, beneficial ownership of 5% holders and insiders, shareholder proposals; often opens with a letter to shareholders
documents.lag_note: filed before the annual meeting, usually within four months of the fiscal year end
documents.tip: Pay is for the last completed fiscal year; say which.

documents.label: Form S-1 and prospectus (424B4)
documents.holds: registration of a first public offering: business, financials for recent years, risk factors, use of proceeds, ownership before and after
documents.lag_note: no fixed schedule; the final prospectus (424B4) is filed at pricing
documents.tip: Amendments (S-1/A) change numbers; use the latest amendment or the 424B4.

documents.label: Forms 20-F, 40-F and 6-K (foreign issuers)
documents.holds: annual report (20-F, 40-F) and interim or event reports (6-K) of non-US companies listed in the US; accounting may be IFRS
documents.lag_note: 20-F is due four months after the fiscal year end; 6-K has no fixed schedule
documents.tip: There is no 10-Q: interim figures arrive in 6-K filings, if at all.

documents.label: Insider and large-holder forms (Form 4, 13F, 13D/G, Form D)
documents.route_when: \b(form 4|insider (?:buying|selling|trading|transactions?)|13F|13D|13G|institutional holdings|hedge fund holdings|form D|private placement|bought shares|sold shares)\b
documents.holds: Form 4: insider trades, filed within two business days. 13F: quarterly holdings of large managers, due 45 days after quarter end. 13D/13G: stakes above 5%. Form D: a private fundraising
documents.lag_note: Form 4 within two business days; 13F within 45 days of quarter end
documents.tip: Transaction date is not filing date.

documents.label: Patent documents and kind codes
documents.holds: A1/A2 = published application (about 18 months after the earliest filing); B1/B2 = granted patent (B1 had no earlier publication, B2 did); US numbers read US 11,234,567 B2; EP and WO numbers carry their own kind codes
documents.lag_note: applications are usually published about 18 months after the priority date, so recent filings are not visible yet
documents.tip: Three dates differ: priority, filing and publication. Ask for the one the question means.

documents.label: Preprints and journal articles
documents.holds: arXiv: the authors' submission, with v1, v2 ... each dated; the abstract page lists the first submission date. Journal articles: the publisher's version of record, with received, accepted and published dates
documents.tip: A preprint and its journal version have different dates; say which.

documents.label: Press releases (wire and company newsroom)
documents.holds: the company's announcement as issued, with a dateline and timestamp; wire services republish it unchanged
documents.lag_note: same day as the event, normally
documents.tip: A news article about the release is second-hand; prefer the release itself.
